chunks: whoever observes excesses being committed and people being called towards evil and disapproves it with his heart is safe and free from responsibility for it,
and whoever disapproves of it with his tongue would be rewarded and he is in a higher position than the former

but whoever disapproves it with his sword in order that the word of Allāh may remain superior and the word of the oppressors may remain inferior, catches hold of the path of guidance and stands on the right way, while his heart is lighted with conviction.

key_terms.مُنْكَر: Evil or that which is disapproved

ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of forbidding evil in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: This passage from Ibn Abī Laylā’s sermon in *Nahj al-Balagha* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf wa Nahi 'an al-Munkar* (Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil) through a graded hierarchy of action. It elevates physical jihad by the sword as the ultimate realization of faith, linking internal conviction with external struggle to establish divine sovereignty over oppression, a concept deeply rooted in early Islamic history and Shia political theology.
